thread:
Alex (Sales): Hey team — OptimaHealth POC is seeing intermittent 429s during load test. Customer sends parallel chat requests (30/min) and hits a hard stop after ~7m. Can someone eyeball tenant: optima-001?

Jamie (Platform SE): Thanks Alex. Do we have the request sample + headers and the exact error payload? 429 body + any X-RateLimit headers would help. Also which model/route are they hitting?

Alex (Sales): Pasted what they sent: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "detail": "per-route cap exceeded"
}
X-RateLimit-Limit: 500
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 12
```

Route: POST /v1/chat/generate (model: redwood-large-extends). They included bursts of 100 concurrent short chats, avg tokens/user ~600 (max_tokens=512 + prompt).

Maria (SRE): Hosting mode? Dedicated vs Hosted matters for how quotas are enforced. Also need tenant internal id (optima-001 ok) and the customer token_budget config — are we applying per-tenant token budgets + per-route caps?

Liam (Support): I can pull logs if you give me the workspace/tenant id (I have access to infra logs). Alex confirmed tenant header is `X-Account-ID: optima-001`. Approving log pull now.

DeployBot: Automated note: ratecap-change-request queued for optima-001. Ticket #SR-9142 created.

Jamie (Platform SE): If they're sending many concurrent short chats with large max_tokens, token accounting will spike. Two immediate mitigations: reduce `max_tokens` in client to 256 OR disable large parallelism (limit concurrent requests). We can also temporarily increase per-route cap for this tenant.

Maria (SRE): Quick check from logs (pulled):
```
2026-03-21T18:10:05Z tenant=optima-001 route=/v1/chat/generate concurrent=98 token_window=600 tokens_consumed=47500 x_rl_limit=500 x_rl_remain=0
2026-03-21T18:10:18Z tenant=optima-001 429 per-route-cap reached
```
Looks like they're exhausting a per-route burst window rather than the monthly token budget. The bucket resets every 60s (burst window).

Jamie (Platform SE): Can we confirm the per-route cap for optima-001? I think default per-route is 500 qps tokens-equivalent. For hosted trials we cap bursts to protect noisy neighbors.

Liam (Support): Confirmed config: per-route cap=500 (token-equivalent units), tenant daily token_budget=2,000,000. They are well under daily budget, so it's burst/per-route.

Alex (Sales): Customer expects to run scaled demo for 2 hours tomorrow. They ask if we can allow higher burst for demo. Sophie can you confirm commercial ok for temporary bump?

Sophie (Account Exec): OptimaHealth is in trial but looking at Dedicated in Q3. I can approve a one-time demo bump if we limit to 2 hours and take monitoring screenshots. Approving temporary bump to 2,500 for 2 hours pending SRE sign-off.

Maria (SRE): I can do that. Proposed plan:
- Temporarily raise per-route cap for tenant optima-001 from 500 -> 2500 for 2 hours starting 2026-03-22T14:00:00Z
- Enable enhanced token sampling (debug) and add a metric alert if error rate >2%
- After window, revert and collect metrics + customer impact notes

Jamie (Platform SE): Also push these customer-side recommendations to reduce TO: max_tokens=256, enable client-side concurrency throttle (max 30 concurrent), and switch to streaming so they don't need huge max_tokens. That should reduce token spikes.

Liam (Support): Done — I've applied the temporary cap bump in the rate-control service and added the debug sampling flags. Patch ID: rc-bump-321. Action log:
```
PATCH /config/tenants/optima-001
set per_route_cap=2500 (ttl=7200s)
set debug.token_sampling=true
```

DeployBot: Config change applied by Liam. ChangeID=rc-bump-321. Audit log updated.

Alex (Sales): Passed the window times and notes to OptimaHealth. They will rerun load at 14:15.

Sophie (Account Exec): Please save CPU/latency graphs, they want to show performance to their CTO.

Maria (SRE): Will monitor. If error rate stays >1.5% after bump we should consider adding a short-term autoscale or advise Dedicated proof-of-concept.

Jamie (Platform SE): Also sending a quick snippet customers can use to limit tokens/concurrency:
```
const limiter = new PQueue({concurrency: 30});
await limiter.add(() => callChat({max_tokens:256, stream:true}));
```

Liam (Support): Follow-up: after bump at 14:00 we saw peak concurrent ~210 and no 429s during the 2h window. Post-bump revert at 16:00 returned cap to 500 and 429s resumed after 4m under same load. Logs & screenshots attached to ticket #SR-9142.

Alex (Sales): Great — customer saw clean demo, CTO asked for Dedicated sizing. Sophie, can you start handoff to AE?

Sophie (Account Exec): On it. I'll open a new internal handoff thread and attach the metrics.

Maria (SRE): Closing ops side. Recommend we add a docs blurb in the POC checklist: warn about token-heavy chats, advise streaming + lower max_tokens, and offer a demo bump process.

Alex (Sales): Thanks all :thumbsup:

Jamie (Platform SE): Nice teamwork. Saved the postmortem notes under internal docs.

Liam (Support): Closing SR-9142 as resolved (pending customer ack).

Sophie (Account Exec): Customer follow-up scheduled for tomorrow 10am PT.

Alex (Sales): Closing thread.
